name: Andon Electronics Corporation
old_description: Andon Electronics Corporation - Innovative Socket Designs For Optimum Device Protection
about:
Andon Electronics Corporation is based in Lincoln, Rhode Island. The company is led by president John O. Tate, who developed the precision semiconductor socket contact that underpins its product line. While the founding year is not publicly disclosed, the business has established itself as a specialist in socket solutions for electronic device placement.

The company manufactures innovative precision sockets used to mount image sensors, optoelectronic sensors, gas sensors, DC‑DC converters, batteries, crystal oscillators, fuses, relays, and other electronic devices onto printed circuit boards. Its catalog spans dozens of package types — including PGA, BGA, LCC, DIP, SIP, TO, PLCC, and LED — as well as specialty items such as heat‑sink sockets, high‑temperature sockets, ultra‑low‑profile sockets, floating‑pin sockets, and laminate wafer sockets. Andon offers both standard and custom socket designs.

Andon’s sockets are used by original equipment manufacturers and contract manufacturers in industries such as camera production, laser manufacturing, gas‑sensing equipment, and broader electronic product assembly. Named customers include Chungwa Telecom Labs and Micropac Industries, indicating a presence in telecommunications and specialized industrial electronics.

The company states that its socket designs help customers avoid device damage during assembly, reduce board‑assembly labor, and improve turnaround time. This focus on device protection and assembly efficiency is presented as the core reason for its product development.
